creator: Alexander Terp
description:
amterp, 2026-10-03: "I think we wanna make all Windows part of one muster process".

Today each window is its own process (3ca8e4bb, 2026-08-30: "Each is its own process, so quitting one leaves the others working"), with its own command socket (`$MUSTER_SOCKET`), its own core, and a shared record of names held under a file lock so two processes agree on what a pane is called. amterp reverses that: one app process, many NSWindows - which is how a Mac app is expected to behave (one Dock icon, cmd+q quits the app, the Window menu lists every window).

What it costs and why that is acceptable now: quitting ends every window at once, but no agent - the daemon owns the PTYs, so a quit costs nothing that a relaunch does not bring back, provided relaunch reopens every window that was open (a_2KAFWbZBa, which this subsumes: quit is not close).

Questions the design has to answer: whether the core holds one view per window or the shell keeps a core per window; one command socket for the app or one per window (every pane already carries `$MUSTER_SOCKET`, and `--socket` is public CLI surface); what becomes of the cross-window machinery (carrying a request to another window, handing a pane over, the names record and its lock) once windows share memory; `muster window new`/`list`/`reopen`; what a running pre-change window process does when a new build launches. Large enough for a MIP (docs/mip/).
title: 🪟 Every window is a window of one Muster process
